rows.Incident Description: Booking misunderstanding
rows.Subject: Spa | Amira AL RAAISI  | Booking misunderstanding
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
On January 1st,  Mr. Blanc booked a duo massage with Mrs Al Raaisi for Saturday,  January 3rd at 6:00 PM. The clients did not attend the appointment. When contacted,  Mr. Blanc stated that he believed the booking was for another date and later acknowledged that he may have made a mistake due to workload.

He was informed that cancellation was not possible under the 24-hour cancellation policy,  and that the correct date was confirmed on the payment record,  email confirmation,  and reminder call. A duo massage could not be offered on the requested Sunday due to practitioner availability. An alternative solution was proposed,  including treatments with the remaining time and complimentary pool access,  which Mr. Blanc declined.

As an exceptional gesture,  the Spa Director agreed to reschedule the massages within January,  with the option of separate appointments,  which Mr. Blanc accepted. Shortly afterward,  Mrs. Al Raaisi arrived at the spa with a friend,  requested a refund,  and refused several proposed options. She mentioned that she personally knew one of the therapist; the Spa Director informed her that the massages would be performed by another practitioner,  to which Mrs. Blanc replied that she was aware. After discussion,  the massages were rescheduled for January 25th,  to be performed consecutively,  with no further modifications allowed. Confirmation was sent to both clients.

Following investigation,  all communications confirmed the appointment date of January 3rd.

Mrs. Al Raaisi sent an email expressing her dissatisfaction (04/10). The Director of Rooms responded with an apology and proposed an alternative time slot for duo treatments along with complimentary pool access. (05.10) Mrs appreciate the feedback and confirmed her booking in duo suite at 4:30 pm.

rows.Incident Description: Guest ordered two Croque Madame sandwiches via room service, which were served lukewarm and overpriced.
rows.Subject: 422 | Mr. Joao Hansen Neto | Billing Issue / Dispute Charge / Pricing
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
In the afternoon,  the guest ordered two Croque Madame sandwiches via Room Service. Since Croque Madame was not listed on the Room Service menu,  the team had to confirm with the kitchen and prepared the bill as requested,  totaling €153 for the two sandwiches. About an hour later,  the guest called to complain that the food was cold and expressed dissatisfaction with the high price of €150 for two sandwiches.

The Assistant Manager went to the guest’s room,  cleared the table,  and  apologized for the overall experience. rows.Incident Description: Spa Massage Experience
rows.Subject: 508 | Mr. Wei Lun Yeh | Spa Mode
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
On the 21st,  the guest contacted GR to express her disappointment regarding a body massage for her mother,  which took place in the evening of the 18th at the Spa.

At the time of booking,  the guest had clearly specified a preference for a deep,  strong massage,  and this information was properly noted in the Spa booking.

However,  according to the guest’s feedback,  her mother did not appreciate the massage at all. She reported that during the first 20 minutes,  the practitioner was only lightly touching her rather than performing an actual massage. The guest also felt that the session ended very quickly and lacked care and attention throughout.

Due to a language barrier,  the guest’s mother was unable to communicate her dissatisfaction directly to the Spa team during the treatment.

Feedback from the Spa:
The guest arrived at the scheduled time for her treatment at 8 p.m.  
The son spent five minutes explaining the type of pressure his mother wanted. 
The practitioner accompanied the guest to the changing room,  and madam came out of the changing room after five minutes.
 Once in the treatment room,  the practitioner asked the guest to sign the consultation card,  but the guest wanted to go back to the changing room to get her phone to call her son. 
The telephone conversation lasted about five minutes.
 The practitioner suggested that the guest begin the massage,  but madam wanted to take a shower.
 The massage began 25 minutes late. 
The practitioner focused on the areas requested by the son,  using strong pressure until the end of the treatment,  which was scheduled for 9 p.m. A 30% discount was applied to the service.

GR apologised to the guest and explained the situation. Guest shown his understanding.  A candle Trvdon was sent to guest as departure gift during TD on the 21st. Guest to be met by Night manager upon departure at 6h on the 22nd.

Guest met upon check out by front desk supervisor. (Chinese speaker)
Guest say that it was a problem of understanding. 
Guest was fine and very happy with his stay. Closed

Guest added that it is unacceptable since it is the second time and asked for the high management email address. It appears that dispatch did not not update the greeter service of the change. Consequently,  the greeter was attending to someone else at that time.

Chabé shall remove the charge of the arrival transfer + offer the departure transfer + ensure measures that it will not occur again.

After being informed that it was in fact the cold salad buffet,  she became frustrated,  saying she could no longer enjoy the dessert selection because she had eaten beef unintentionally.

The Lobby Manager apologized again and offered a complimentary brunch for one of the guests. Madam and Sir were satisfied but presented a Givex card to settle the remaining brunch.Therefore,  the Givex card was used for both brunches,  and the guests have been invited back on another date to enjoy a LiLi Brunch complimentary as a gesture of goodwill.

rows.Subject: Le Lobby Restaurant | Mr. Khalid Al Deghaither | Service
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The guest arrived at the Lobby at 10:50 a.m. and requested to have breakfast. The Assistant Manager politely informed him that he could be welcomed in the Lobby,  but that the kitchen was closed and that the restaurant would be preparing to welcome brunch guests starting at 12:00 p.m.

The Assistant Manager reassured the guest by explaining that teas,  coffees,  fruit juices,  and pastries could be served. The guest accepted this proposal. Additionally,  the guest was informed that in-room breakfast was also available.

Subsequently,  the guest was informed that he could remain at the table for approximately one hour and that a table would be reserved for him at the bar at any time if needed. The guest then strongly expressed his dissatisfaction and repeatedly insisted on speaking with the General Manager.

The Director of Rooms was informed,  followed by the intervention of the Director of Guest Experience,  who met with the guest in order to find a solution.

Following the recommendation of the Director of Guest Experience,  the Assistant Manager apologized to the guest and kindly offered the breakfast as a gesture of goodwill. Some patries and coffees were offered.

The guest then expressed himself,  stating: "You know,  as a hotel guest,  it’s like we own the hotel and you are my employee,  so you must adapt to all my requests and needs."

The Assistant Manager listened to the guest and did not engage further with this statement. The guest eventually left satisfied and exited the restaurant,  thanking the Assistant Manager.

rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The guests came to have lunch in the Lobby at 1.00 p.m. In the middle of their meal,  after finishing her main course,  the lady felt unwell. She lost consciousness and slumped in her chair.

The security team responded within 20 seconds,  as did the Lobby managers. The lady was moved to the Etoile lounge and placed in the recovery position. Security then took over alongside the emergency services. She was subsequently taken to hospital by ambulance.

We have since received news. Apparently,  there is nothing to report and the lady is well. The Maître d’Hôtel had duly checked whether the lady had any allergies when taking the order. The lady also reconfirmed that she had no allergies once she had regained consciousness.

It was not a case of food poisoning either,  as all the guests had the same dishes and only the lady felt unwell. 

Following this incident,  the family left for the hospital without finishing their meal. The full bill was waived. No follow-up needed.

rows.Incident Description: Train Station Arrival Transfer – last minute cancellation fees complaint
rows.Subject: Reception Desk | Mr. Dave Kamin | Chabe
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Upon check-out the guest complained of a charge of 185 euros regarding a last-minute cancellation fees of a private driver transportation that was requested by his PA on February 15th for a pick up at Gare de Lyon February 15th at 1.30pm and cancelled by the PA.
Guest was met by Deputy Head Concierge.
Guest was unhappy about this and does not understand why he got charged as it seems that from once the car was confirmed until the PA cancelled was short time.
Deputy Head Concierge understood the guest frustration and was sorry about the situation,  he kindly explained to the guest that the transfer was an urgent last-minute requested by his PA and the PA agreed with the late charge.
Deputy Head Concierge also kindly reminded that the Limousine Company has a strict cancellation policy of 3 hours and the driver was already reserved.
Guest threatened that he was going to write a review on Trip Advisor.
Deputy Head Concierge proposed that we will contact Chabe and try to find a solution.
Chabe answered that the cancellation was received after 25 minutes once the service was confirmed.
Deputy Head Concierge will contact Chabe Hospitality Sales Manager to find a solution if they can do a gesture or 50 % off reduction. 
DHC will contact the guest once we received a final response from Chabe.
17-02- Chabe offered 50% which is 92.50 euros + e-mail sent to the guest  by Deputy Head Concierge 
*******************************************
In the meantime results of the investigations: 
15-02 at 12.38pm requested from PA received by e-mail at the Concierge
15-02 at 12.53pm e-mail response sent by concierge asking for further information.
15-02 at 12.58 pm the PA replied saying that this is urgent. 
15-02 at around1pm Chabe dispatch contacted to find a last minute and reserve a vehicle.
15-02 at 01.06pm concierge sent an e-mail confirmation with cancellation policy. 
15-02 at 01.08pm The PA reconfirm this saying please pick them up,  confirmed.
15-02 at 1.13pm – The PA sent an e-mail saying sorry,  but the guest changed his mind.
15-02 at 1.19pm – The Concierge replied and kindly reminded that the service cannot be cancelled and asked to the PA if she still wants to proceed with the cancellation even if fees are involved ( Chabe was contacted and they refused to cancel it as they have already sent the driver) 
15-02- 1.25pm – The PA replied saying: Yes cancel it anyway 
15-02 1.29pm – Concierge confirms the cancellation.

rows.Subject: 506 | Mr. Stanislas Jules Roger Vilgrain | Laundry
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Guets came to Reception to complain that the feathers in their down jacket are unevenly distributed after the cleaning.
Apologies extended to the guest.
Front desk took the jacket to the laundry to dry it and then returned it to the client.

After investigation,  we found that the down jacket had not been dried sufficiently,  which caused the feathers not to redistribute properly.

Chocolate box and note offered in the room.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Implement a laundry quality-control step to ensure items are fully dried and checked before being returned to guests.

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained that the room was not cleaned after coming back at 16:30
rows.Subject: 506 | Mr. Stanislas Jules Roger Vilgrain | Service Delay
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Guest complained to front desk that the room was not cleaned after coming back at 16:30.
Apologies extended.

As soon as the room was not on DND anymore,  Housekeeper started to clean the room.

After investigation,  the room was on Do Not Disturb until 16:28. Guest was aware about it and was fine.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Reinforce clear coordination between Front Desk and Housekeeping so rooms are cleaned promptly once the Do Not Disturb sign is removed.

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained about check out process being too long, and lack of coordination between the reception team members
rows.Subject: Reception Desk | Ms. Anastassiya Zhomartova | Check Out Process Delay
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Guests replied to their final invoice email,  mentioning their disappointment with their checkout experience on the 11th of March. Guest mentioned that they informed the reception team 40 minutes in advance of their planned checkout and expected everything to be prepared while they were having brunch. When they returned,  the staff member they had spoken with was no longer available,  and another colleague had to restart the entire process,  causing an additional 15‑minute delay. This lack of coordination also affected their driver,  who had to wait,  as well as the staff assisting with their luggage.

FDM sent an apology email,  offering the incidentals amounting 127.80€ as well as a complimentary upgrade for next stay. guest replied to the email,  mentioning that she really appreciated our guest oriented approach,  and will definitely come back in August with family.

Investigation ongoing with reception team. Investigation will be finished on 18.03
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Ensure a simple checkout handover so any reception colleague can complete the process without delay.

rows.Incident Description: Guest arrived earlier at the airport with a Chabe greeter but could not check in due to airline boarding timing
rows.Subject: 531 | Ms. Kai Liu | Chabe
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Guest asked the Concierge team if she could leave 5 hours prior to her flight departure due at 19h30 with Air China in Business class.
She had a Chabe greeter to expedite check in and taxes refund. She left at 14h to CDG.
Regrettably due to a miscommunication,  guest arrived at 15h30 and check in were all closed until 16h30. Air China boarding rules.
Guest contacted the Chinese speaker in Reception to express her disappointement.
Apologies extended by the Chinese speaker receptionist and a free upgrade offered for her next stay.
Guest was really appreciative.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Ensure the Concierge clearly confirms airline check‑in opening times and earliest recommended airport arrival before arranging departure transfers.

rows.Incident Description: Guest called concierge and complained about AC issue in the room.
rows.Subject: 417 | Mr. Nitin Goyal | AC Issue
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Guest called concierge at around 10pm and complained about AC issue. The room was too hot and the ventilation not working.
Engineering was immediately sent to the room and could not fix the issue.
Night Manager was made aware and called guest to apologize for the inconvenience and suggested a room move to another room or two Dyson fans as alternative.
Guest declined the room move but accepted if we could bring him two fans. Housekeeping was called to do the needful.
Guest met by FDM upon check out on 18/03 - 55€ for minibar and laundry waived as gesture + gift offered upon departure.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Ensure clear escalation and quick temporary solutions (fans or room move) when a technical issue cannot be fixed immediately.

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained about the price of the plate of exotic fruit ordered through room service
rows.Subject: Reception Desk | Ms. Mary Margaret Mc Donnell | Billing Issue / Dispute Charge / Pricing
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
At checkout,  the guest was surprised by the price of the exotic fruit platter she had ordered on March 18. 
Price: 40 euros 

The guest had placed her order using the note she had left on her doorknob.
The guest had part of her breakfast covered by her FHR credit. As a gesture of goodwill,  the additional charge of 13.38 euros was waived as a gesture.
Guest was thankful 

Update: The document to be placed on the doorknob states that guests can find the prices of the products on the tablet.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Remind guests that prices are available in the tablet for breakfast orders.

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained about coffee machine and phones not working as well as lights flickering in the bathroom. She also mentioned that the room was too dark
rows.Subject: 119 | Mrs. Jenny Yu | Overall Incident
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Upon check out,  guest complained about coffee machines and phones not working in both rooms 119 and 116. Guest also mentioned that lights were flickering in the bathroom of 119 and the rooms were too dark.
coffee machines not working: Guest did not inform us about it during the stay. Verification has been made after check out,  and there was indeed an issue with coffee machines. Coffee machines have been fixed
Phones not working: Glitch IC-00421-001 already logged during the stay 
Lights flickering in the bathroom: Guest showed a video to FDM where the lights were indeed flickering. As per IT,  the issue is happening in few rooms due to the spots being not compatible with the actual program. FUP with IT and ENG to fix the issue
Room too dark: Profile updated for next stay to allocate a room on high floor

Apologies extended by FDM upon check out. Upgrade for next stay has been offered and business card given.

Agence: Bank of America
Rate per night: 810€
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Ensure all room equipment and lighting are proactively checked before arrival, with technical issues escalated and resolved promptly between IT and Engineering.

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained that the salmon for her dogs was not flaked enough
rows.Subject: 541 | Mr. Keith Tyler Kosow | Dislike Food / Beverage Preparation
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
- Guest complained that the salmon for her dogs was not flaked enough
- Apologies extended; kitchen prepared two new portions,  which were provided free of charge
- Guest requested to keep the two original portions for later
- Guest met by DGR at the breakfast following this incident. Guest appreciative for the follow up and quick resolution
- Guest profile updated accordingly 
Closer
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Standardize pet meal preparation instructions in the guest profile and kitchen checklist to ensure dietary preferences are consistently followed.

rows.Incident Description: Guest disapointed of diner at Restaurant Blandine on March, 17th
rows.Subject: Concierge Desk | Mr. Glenn Koh | Bad Recommendations
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
On March 17th the guest complained at the Concierge Desk about the restaurant Blandine that was reserved by the concierge team for a diner on March,  17th for 5 people at 8.30pm.
The guest mentioned with some photos as a proof that a spiders’ web was found on a lamp and the chicken of the cesar salad was overcooked and the bacon was non.
Apologies extended by Assistant Concierge 
On March 18th apologies message was sent by Deputy Head Concierge 
Mrs Ho was thankful for the following up and added that this diner was supposed to be for celebrate their 12 years old birthday’s daughter ( which was not mentioned when requesting for a recommendation),  the food was quite careless and she found the dining room was poorly maintained.
Besides this experience,  Mrs. Koh emphasized that the family were very happy with assistance from the Peninsula Concierge team during their stay.
Following up on going with the restaurant in order to make sure that an improvement on the daily maintain of the restaurant will be assured by the restaurant.
Head Concierge will contact Mr. Koh as Mrs. Koh has already left the hotel with the children.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Ensure that the recommendation is made according to the exact guest needs and expectations before reserving.

rows.Incident Description: Guest's PA informed DGR that telephone in the room did not work properly
rows.Subject: 410 | Mrs. Leena Kumar Nair | Telephone
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Apologies extended by DGR.
According to the guest the telephone did not work at all in living room & only rang in bedroom part but she could not hear anything.
Suggestion of an ITEELV intervention prior to guest departure.
PA preferred we wait & do intervention after C/O at 10:30am.
IT team resolved the issue right after.
Informative glitch closed
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: pre-arrival checks to ensure IT and technical issues are  resolved

rows.Subject: Item in the breakfast IDR not prepared as requested
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
- Guest reported via PenChat that the breakfast omelette had not been prepared according to the order instructions
- The guest had requested the cheese,  mushrooms,  and sausage to be mixed into the omelette,  but they were served on the side instead
- He specified that the dish did not need to be remade and wished only to provide feedback

- Apologised extended for the inconvenience 
- Guest met in his room to apologize with one chocolate box and in order to clean the table 
- Guest appreciative for the follow up 

- Internal investigation revealed that there was a misreading on the doorknob by room service order taker regarding the instructions made
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Reinforce room‑service order procedures and clearly highlight special instructions on doorknob orders to avoid misinterpretation.

rows.Incident Description: Guest expressed his disappointment to DGR following a new incident involving food amenities & his dogs.
rows.Subject: 541 | Mr. Keith Tyler Kosow | Amenities Delivery
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
2 days ago one of his dogs had been hospitalized after ingesting grapes from the room amenities. 
Following this,  instructions were passed to remove grapes during the stay (cf glitch on 18.03 IC-00432-001)
Today guest reported that macarons & madeleines had been placed in the room & he believed he had communicated that no amenities or sugary items should be provided at all. His dogs consumed the macarons which he described as a real danger. He is now monitoring their condition to determine whether another emergency veterinary visit will be necessary.
DGR apologized & explained that the instruction received had only been to remove grapes,  not all food items. 
Guest stated that he is very disappointed & believes such precautions should be automatic whenever a guest stays with dogs (no sugar ame or to cover them)
All amenities have been removed until departure & bottle champagne grand cru offered with note from DGR. 
To be met again upon c/o on 20.03.

Guest was met by AFDM and DFO upon check out
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Place guest amenities secured (sous cloche) or elevated areas inaccessible to pets

rows.Incident Description: Guest was disappointed about the product and hairdryer used.
rows.Subject: 440 | Mrs. Liraz Nikfard | Hair service Quality
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The client had an appointment scheduled at 1:00 PM and arrived at 1:15 PM. At approximately 1:45 PM,  the service was done and when she met the receptionnist,  she informed that she did not wish to pay the full amount for the service.

The assistant manager met with the client,  who stated that she was dissatisfied with her experience. She mentioned that the products used had no noticeable fragrance,  that the hairstylist appeared slow in her movements,  and that the hairdryer did not seem professional. 

After investigation,  it was confirmed that the products used have a mild fragrance and that the hairdryer,  although compact,  is professional-grade. However,  these did not meet the client’s expectations.

We apologized to the client and recorded her preferences for future visits. A 15% discount was applied to the final bill. The client paid €153 instead of €180. The hairstylist’s compensation for the service was €135.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1:
The hairdresser should explain the products used to put the guest at ease. 
They should also explain that we use the latest hairdryer technology to reduce noise and protect the hair.
If a customer prefers a traditional hairdryer, we have one in stock for them to use.

rows.Incident Description: The guest requested service at 7:10 PM, and at 7:30 PM the guest called asking why nobody had come yet
rows.Subject: 306 | Mr. Abdulaziz Bader A Alyahya | Service Delay
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The guest requested service at 7:10 PM,  and at 7:30 PM the guest called asking why nobody had come yet.
 Apologies were extended. 
A room attendant arrived at the door at 7:39 PM,  but the guest had the DND sign on. 
The guest was called back to inform them about the DND status,  and service was started at 7:50 PM. Two room attendants were sent.

Please ensure attentive care is provided until departure,  particularly for all requested hsk/rs services.
CLOSED
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Ensure DND status is checked and confirmed with the guest before dispatching housekeeping or room service to avoid delays.

rows.Incident Description: the 2 Connecting doors between rooms 237 and 238 not locked

SNM noticed that on the connecting door on the side of the room 237,  the lock was closed with one turn and that to lock the door you have to turn twice the lock.

Both guests in room 237 + 238 have checked in today March 19th,  2026 but aren't travelling together.
In house guest in room 237 didn't report any missing items.

Courtesy call to be made on March 20th 2026

Guest contacted 20/03 but unreachable
Champagne Deutz + Selection of cheese + apology note were placed in the room
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Ensure all connecting doors are double‑locked during check‑in checks, with verification included in the room inspection checklist.

rows.Incident Description: Several rooms encountering Tablet issues to order Room Service : #301 + 238 + 436

#301 Mrs Selfe

 All other departments were also notified to exercise increased caution.

rows.Incident Description: leaking iron, shower leak.
rows.Subject: 106 | Mr. Rafael Ramirez Cerejido | Several issue in the room
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The guest complained several issues to GR: the iron in their room was leaking on the day they arrived,  the water in the shower flows very slowly causing it to leak onto the floor,  and the sink plug in the bathroom is not functioning properly.

GR apologized to the guest. As the guest preferred not to change rooms,  GR promised to address all these issues in their room during their absence in the afternoon by maintenance team and will arrange for champagne and an apology note to be sent to the room.

AFDM/GR should contact the guest via WhatsApp later in the evening to provide an update,  as requested by the guest.

Departure gift is prepared for departure on the 21/03

Guest was met by DFO upon return at the hotel,  cocktails were offered at the bar 
Guest unreachable on the evening,  to be met on 21.03

Met by AFDM upon C/O - They had a wonderful stay
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Carry out quick maintenance checks and fix reported issues immediately, with a brief follow-up to the guest to confirm resolution.

rows.Incident Description: Complained the shower was flooded and no one fixed it although he reported the issue
rows.Subject: 438 | Mr. Stephen James Orava | 1 Incident Case
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Guest came at the front desk at 11:50am to report that his shower was flooded and to ask someone to fix the drainage.
FD agent created a HotSOS at 11:54 and it was completed by engineering at 12:20.
Guest came back to the FD at 15:00 and complained that it was not fixed and that his room had not been serviced.
FD apologized and created a new ticket for the shower and for the service.
Engineering manager and AHH confirmed the problem was fixed
DFO gave courtesy call to extend apologies and guest was grateful
Guest left in a good spirit and enjoyed his stay with us.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Ensure engineering confirms full resolution and housekeeping completion before closing tickets, with a follow-up check before guest returns to the room.

rows.Incident Description: Breakfast inclusion and noise from Rue de la Pérousse
rows.Subject: 119 | Mr. Sohar Zeharia Flisfisch | Overall Incident
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The guest was surprised to see an additional charge of 82 euros for breakfast,  stating that he had not been informed of this. 
He also mentioned being disturbed by noise (on the Rue Pérouse side) on the morning of March 20,  caused by trucks. 

Apologies offered by the front desk supervisor
€82 deduction applied for the breakfast charge
Profile updated to assign a quiet room in the future
Final invoice sent by email with upgrade offered for next reservation
rows.Feedback Remarks 1:
- Clearly inform guests of breakfast pricing at check-in 
- prioritize assigning quieter rooms to avoid noise disturbances.

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained about bad smell coming from the bathroom
rows.Subject: 105 | Ms. Jaclyn Goldberger | Abnormal Smell / Odour
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
In the morning,  the guest complained about a bad odor in her bathroom. 
A Hotsos ticket was created at 10:49 a.m. and closed at 12:02 p.m.

In the afternoon,  the guest asked to speak to a manager. 
The duty manager called the guest,  who reported that the odor was still present in the bathroom. 
The duty manager met with the guest and offered to move her to room 108 (the guest wished to stay on the first floor). 
The guest declined the room change and preferred to stay in room 105 but guest was thankful. 

She requested that the issue be taken care of while she went to dinner. 
A bottle of champagne and 4 bottles of sparkling water were delivered by room service as a gesture (the guest likes sparkling water)
Courtesy call to be made on 21.03 to ensure that guest is satisfied with the new intervention 

Guest contacted by phone and apologies extended room move suggested but declined. guest confirmed everything is fine. 


Met by AFDM,  was thankful for the follow up 
CLOSED
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: follow‑up and recheck procedure after the first intervention to ensure odors or maintenance issues are fully resolved before guest returns to the room.

rows.Guest Name: Mrs. Azizah Saeed A Al Haddal

rows.Incident Description: The guest complained about: the response time of the concierges, the price quoted for a transfer to Courchevel, missing items in a room service order, and the price for luggage transfer to another Parisian hotel
rows.Subject: Reception Desk | Mr. Guillaume Jenner | Overall Incident
rows.Investigation Remarks 1: The guest complained about: the response time of the concierges,  the price quoted for a transfer to Courchevel,  missing items in a room service order,  and the price for luggage transfer to another Parisian hotel
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Improve response time, ensure clear pricing, and double-check services before delivery.

rows.Incident Description: Complained about cigarette smell on the 4th floor
rows.Subject: Guest Corridor 4th Floor | Mr. Robert Boghossian | Abnormal Smell / Odour
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Guest complained to front desk supervisor that their was a cigarette smell in the corridor of the 4th floor 
Apologies extended by FD supervisor who promised to the guest a follow up 
ENG informed about this (recurrent) issue 
Departure gift prepared for departure. to be met upon departure

Guest complained again about cigarette smell on 4th floor. 
Unfortunately duty manager was not available at this time and then guest was unreachable

Investigation: AGG went to the room,  and could not find any bad smell in the toilets
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Monitor corridors more frequently and act immediately on odor reports, with clear follow-up and escalation if the issue persists.

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained to Room attendant that the room was dusty and that his breakfast ordered this morning on arrival was not removed
rows.Subject: 528 | Mr. Arthur Lemami | Cleanliness
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
At 21:00,  the guest complained to the Room Attendant that the room was dusty and that the breakfast tray from his early‑morning arrival had not been removed.
AGG called the guest immediately to gather more details:
- The guest explained that he has stayed at the hotel several times and found the cleanliness below his expectations on this occasion. He reported that the bathroom,  bedroom,  and reading lights were very dusty.
-He also mentioned that when he returned at 19:00,  his breakfast tray was still in the room (from his early arrival that morning).
INVESTIGATION and RECOVERY 
- Guest is asking for a deep cleaning tomorrow 
- RS is investigating internally. RS offered new fruits,  macaron and champagne
-Update: 21/03 
Guest was contacted by phone. He confirmed that everything is impeccable today,  in contrast to the previous days,  and expressed his gratitude for the service provided.
Closed
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Ensure thorough daily room inspections, prompt tray removal, and immediate deep cleaning when cleanliness issues are reported.

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained about : delay of answer from concierge, price for luggage's transport to Courchevel, item missing from room service order, price for luggage transport to Cheval Blanc Paris
rows.Subject: Reception Desk | Mr. Guillaume Jenner | Overall Incident
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The guest approached the concierge desk and asked to speak with a manager. 

The duty manager met with the guest,  who wished to provide constructive feedback on her experience at the hotel (a regular at Cheval Blanc Paris): 
- The concierges took too long to respond to her emails 
- The price for a Paris-Courchevel transfer for luggage's was twice as high as what she had been quoted by Cheval Blanc for the same request. (4000 euros)
- She was asked to pay 135 euros to have her luggage (1p) transferred to Cheval Blanc Paris (whereas Cheval Blanc charges 10 euros for this service)
- Items were missing from her room service order
She therefore indicated that she really liked the hotel but that these issues would prevent her from returning. 

RS internal investigation revealed that there was no Room-Service order placed by the guests throughout their stay (no RS charge posted on the room)

Apology offered by AFDM,  who informed that he will contact her tomorrow regarding her feedback.
Recovery to be discussed. 
It seems that Madame left today. Monsieur will leave tomorrow. 

met upon check-out by DFO and AHC - Breakfast overage waived
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Head concierge had contacted Head Concierge at Cheval Blanc in order to check if rates were accurate as the one quoted by Chabe wich was the case.

rows.Incident Description: Black out not closing
rows.Subject: 632 | Mr. Bruce Dennis Trego | Blackout / Curtain
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Guest called the Front Desk at 11:26 PM on March 20th as his blackout wasn't closing.
Apologies extended by Night Auditor to the guest and Night Technician sent to the room.

Night Technician couldn't solve definitely the issue.
A reset was done but each time the black out was closed,  it was reopening immediately. The only solution found was for tonight to disconnect electrical the black out.

Follow up to be done on March 21st to solve the issue by ELV

Guest contacted and they mentioned that everything is working correctly 
they request extra water and it was sent. 

Closed 

update of 24/03: Met by Night manager,  honey offered,  guest appreciative but mentioned that the panel still was not working after few days. Apologies extended.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Ensure technical issues are fully fixed and tested promptly, not temporarily reset.

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained that no table of 8 was available
rows.Subject: 509 | Mr. Emad Ibrahim B Al Omani | Breakfast Inclusion
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The guest arrived at approximately 9:00 AM at the lobby restaurant requesting their reserved table. 
No reservation was recorded and,  due to high occupancy,  no table for 8 guests was immediately available. Two separate tables were initially proposed.

The guest expressed dissatisfaction,  stating that a daily reservation until departure had been promised by the Guest Relations team.

Following reorganization,  a large table with sofa seating was arranged,  meeting the guest’s expectations. Complimentary items were offered as a gesture of goodwill.

Reservations have now been secured for each day until the guest’s departure on March 24.

After investigation with Guest Relations,  no prior reservation had been recorded,  and only breakfast inclusion was confirmed at check in and a whatsapp message was sent to the guest to confirm that breakfast was included.

The guest left satisfied. Extra attention will be provided during breakfast service until departure.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1:
-Record all reservations immediately and reconfirm them with the guest.
- for groups and parties more than 8 guests, ask the guest at check in if they want a table to be booked for breakfast.

rows.Incident Description: Guest placed through the tablet a green peas soup order and found out there is chicken in it
rows.Subject: 240 | Mr. Paul David Meyer Abitbol | Room Tablet Order
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
On March 21st 2026 at 09:00 PM after being served at 08:55 PM,  guest called the room service to ask if in her green peas soup order she placed through the tablet from the Lili menu at 08:27 PM there is chicken as he doesn't eat chicken.
The answer was yes.
Guest asked to have it removed form his bill and didn't want to have it replaced with another soup despite the offer.

Follow up to be made by F&B Management on March 22nd :
Ingredients of the dish updated on both the tablet and the IRD menu.

Guest was met by AFDM upon check out. 
Enjoy his stay especially his spa treatment 
CLOSED
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: list all dish ingredients on the tablet and menu to avoid dietary misunderstandings.

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained about AC not working in the room (room too hot)
rows.Subject: 128 | Ms. Yael Aziza Taqqu | AC Issue
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Guest called front desk on 22.03 morning,  complaining about AC not working (room too hot) in the room since the previous day. Technician tried to make the intervention on the 22.03 at 11pm,  however could not fix the issue from the basement. Guest did not spend a good night since room was too warm. Guest will be leaving the hotel at 2pm on 22.03. Intervention to be made in the room after that time. Apologies extended by FDM,  fan offered in the meantime but guest declined. 

VIP check engineering was made prior to arrival

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained about breakfast overage
rows.Subject: 532 | Ms. Claire Hu | Breakfast Inclusion
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Upon check out,  guest complained about breakfast overage amounting a total of 521€. Guest said that upon check in,  she understood that she had an allowance of 148€ per person per day,  and not 148€ in total per day. 

Investigation: Front desk supervisor who made the check in,  clearly informed the guest upon check in that the allowance was 148€ in total for 2 guests per day. Guest understood it differently. As a gesture,  the 521€ of overage has been waived off.

Improvement: It seems that there is no written mention of the breakfast inclusion on the confirmation letter received by the guest. @reservation department to refine the confirmation letter
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: State the breakfast allowance in writing on the confirmation letter to avoid misunderstanding at check‑in.

rows.Incident Description: The guest reported that she noticed this morning that several pills were missing from her medication box
rows.Subject: 322 | Mr. Joel Stuart Sandler | Missing Item In Guest Room
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The guest reported that she noticed this morning that several pills were missing from her medication box
The guest appeared very stressed and was unable to provide any explanation for the missing pills (photo attached).
The Concierge team is currently assisting her in replacing the medication.
the medications were purchased on 22.03 and delivered to Mrs Sandler’s room - guest was really pleased
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: It is recommended to remind guests, when appropriate, to use in-room safes for storing personal and medical items. Housekeeping procedures should also emphasize vigilance when servicing occupied rooms, ensuring that guest belongings are not moved or handled unnecessarily.

rows.Incident Description: Guest found a moldy fruit in her pastry
rows.Subject: 115 | Ms. Carly Olivia Rademacher | Amenities Not Replenished
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Upon delivering a room-service lunch order to the meeting room,  the organizer of the group mentioned to DBOH that one of her guests found that one of her pastry amenity was moldy.
Sincere apologies were immediately extended by DBOH to both the guest and the organizer of the stay,  and a full refresh was promptly delivered to the room.

Internal investigation revealed that the pastry was placed in the room yesterday prior to guest's arrival and an amenity refresh was planned for today. Due to DND sign being turned on in the morning,  cleaning and refresh service couldn't be made until then. rows.Incident Description: Guest's luggage was taken by another guest

rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
At approximately 10:45 AM,  Mrs. Chen,  assistant to Mr. Yao,  arrived at the hotel for a short visit and left her suitcase with us during her time on the property.
At the same time,  while the valet was accompanying Mrs. Chen to the reception,  another guest,  Mr. Joho (Room #227),  was departing the hotel with his luggage and two chauffeurs. One of the chauffeurs,  mistakenly believing that Mrs. Chen's suitcase belonged to his client,  took it and placed it in their vehicle.
Upon the bellman’s return,  the suitcase was no longer present in front of the hotel entrance.
The guest whose chauffeur mistakenly took the suitcase is still staying at the hotel for another night.
Mr Joho was unsuccessfully contacted by email and phone. The phone numbers on file do not appear to be correct.

The Guest Services Supervisor and the Manager immediately investigated the situation upon noticing that the suitcase was missing.
The guest whose chauffeur mistakenly took the suitcase was identified and confirmed that he is still staying at the hotel.
In parallel,  several attempts to contact Mr. Joho by phone and email were made; however,  the contact details provided appear to be incorrect.
Attempt to use the license plates of Mr. Joho’s two vehicles to identify the rental companies to which they belong,  in the hope of obtaining the chauffeurs’ contact details,  but without success.
At the same time,  Mrs. Chen was kept informed of the progress of the situation.

Update 11:40PM:
Mr Joho's assistants came back with the suitcase.
AFDM met them to obtain more information: chauffeur took the bag as he thought it was belonging to the group (an entire group (guests not staying at PPR) was flying with Mr Joho to Amsterdam by private jet. The group was staying there,  only Mr Joho had to return to Paris)
Once in Amsterdam,  they realized the bag didn't belong to them. Mr Joho and his assistants came back with it.
They apologized for the situation.
Mrs Chen was informed by AFDM that her bag was back in the hotel,  in a safe place. She will come to pick it up on 08.04 morning when she will have breakfast with Penkey Mr Yao (#527).

Update of 09/04:
Guest was met by Night Manager and bag was given back,  gift given by the hotel as gesture to apologize once again for the inconvenience. Guest was very appreciative. Case closed.

rows.Subject: Le Lili | Arthur Lavaud | Food / Beverage Service Delay

Mr Lavaud came to have dinner at the Lili restaurant with his family. The dinner went very well,  and his wife was very happy with the portions of the food served. She thanked the team members each time the dishes were presented.

When the assistant manager approached the table to propose desserts,  Mr Lavaud mentioned that something had already been ordered. The assistant manager then checked with the team,  as nothing had been indicated in the reservation. Unfortunately,  no one was aware of any celebration or dessert request.

Meanwhile,  Mr Lavaud expressed his frustration to the maître d’hôtel,  stating that it was not possible that this had been forgotten. He then requested the bill and moved to the bar to have a drink and a cigar.

The assistant manager gathered the team and discovered that Mr Lavaud had discreetly mentioned to one of the collaborators that it was his son’s birthday. Due to a miscommunication,  this information had not been shared with the rest of the team.

The assistant manager then prepared an Easter creation (chocolate egg amenity) accompanied by traditional chinese buns and candles,  and brought it to the bar to celebrate the client’s son’s birthday. Mr Lavaud and his family were pleasantly surprised seeing the easter creation and thanked the manager of Lili.

rows.Incident Description: External guest complained about slow and inattentive service at the LiLi restaurant (delayed order taking, missing sauces, no dessert menu), guest was disappointed with the overall experience, declined recovery offered by management, and left calm but unlikely to return.
rows.Subject: F&B Non In house guest | Anna  Cloutier  | Food / Beverage Service Delay at LiLi
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Guest complained about overall slow service during dinner on the terrace at LiLi on April 9,  2026.

Guest stated they had to ask multiple times for their order to be taken. Guest complained that requested sauces never arrived at the table. Guest also mentioned that the dessert menu was not proposed. Guest further noted having seen a sommelier crossing the terrace while on a phone call,  which was perceived as inappropriate for a palace setting. Guest was disappointed with the overall dining experience. Madam in particular expressed dissatisfaction at the very last moment while crossing the restaurant to collect her coat,  and shared negative feedback with the hostess upon departure,  which is when the team became aware of all issues,  after the bill had already been settled.

Manager was informed and immediately apologized to the guests. Manager attempted a recovery by inviting the guests to return to the terrace for complimentary desserts and hot beverages; however,  guests were already leaving and declined the offer. Due to the timing of the complaint after payment,  no adjustment or commercial gesture could be applied to the bill.
The LiLi manager confirmed to the guests that the F&B direction would follow up directly with them.
Guests left calm but disappointed and indicated they are unlikely to return due to the overall experience.
Internal investigation is currently underway. The Director of LiLi will personally contact the guests tomorrow (10.04) to follow up and propose an appropriate recovery gesture.

10.04 The Director of LiLi contacted the guest by both phone and email to extend his sincere apologies once again. He also shared his direct contact number should the guest wish to return to LiLi and trust us again; a gesture will be offered on that occasion.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1:
Following this incident, a formal reminder has been issued to the LiLi team, with a renewed emphasis on SOP compliance and service sequences. Particular focus has been placed on reinforcing LQA and Peninsula standards, including maintaining proper eye contact, taking orders within ten minutes, and systematically presenting the dessert menu at the end of the meal.

Teams have been reminded of the importance of adhering to these service fundamentals to prevent recurrence of such issues. Additional emphasis has been placed on proactive communication with managers, ensuring that any service shortcomings are identified and addressed in real time, allowing for corrective action before guest departure.

rows.Incident Description: Lack of kids' amenities

He specifically mentioned that he had expected bath items such as a floating duck,  as previously experienced at PLN and other Palace hotels in Paris.

GR apologized for the inconvenience and offered the children a mini Peninsula bear and coloring materials to enhance their stay. The guest was pleased to receive these additional amenities.

As the guest is departing tomorrow,  he does not expect to receive a floating duck for this evening. However,  GR will arrange a special in-room children’s setup during their outing to create a pleasant surprise upon their return.

Children’s toiletries have since been delivered to the room by Housekeeping. Extra care for TD.
Kids' bathrobes will be offered to guest during TD as gift from HSK.

Internal follow-up:
A trace indicating the arrangement of children’s amenities (toiletries) was recorded in the reservation and marked as completed. However,  the guest did not perceive that these items had been placed in the room. As the arrival was on the 7th,  we are unable to verify whether the amenities were properly set up upon arrival.

Case closed. Guest to be met upon departure.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: We will take extra care when guests are traveling with children under 10 years old, as they may be more sensitive to children's toiletries and amenities.

The manager will personally take care of the guest the following day and extend an additional commercial gesture.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: The Lobby Manager spoke with the Pastry Sous Chef to ensure faster communication between the Lobby team and the pastry team. On their side, the pastry team will be more vigilant in monitoring the proper functioning of the order ticket printers.

rows.Incident Description: Complain about the ingredient in the pea soup
rows.Subject: Le Lili | Mr. Mahmood Ahmadu | Dietary Restriction / Allergy
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
A guest at the table ordered pea soup and specifically inquired whether it contained only seafood. The waiter informed the guest that the soup included crab meat and that the base could be prepared without meat upon request.

After the soup was served,  the guest tasted it and identified the presence of chicken in the base. The guest complained to the waiter and requested to speak with the manager.

The manager attended the table promptly,  listened to the concern,  and clarified the situation. It was identified that the recipe for the soup had recently been changed,  leading to miscommunication among the team regarding its ingredients.

To resolve the issue,  the manager offered to remake the soup according to the guest’s preference and provided complimentary starters as a gesture of goodwill.

The service team maintained attentive and proactive care for the table for the remainder of the visit to ensure guest satisfaction. The guests ultimately left satisfied with the resolution.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1:
The management team of Lili, in collaboration with the Head Chef, will conduct a debrief to review the composition and preparation of the pea soup. This discussion will focus on clarifying the exact ingredients and ensuring consistency in the recipe.

As a result, the description and composition of the dish will be updated to accurately reflect its ingredients. All relevant menus and internal documentation will be revised accordingly, and the service team will be briefed to ensure clear and accurate communication with guests moving forward.

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained about noise coming from the corridor
rows.Subject: 530 | Mr. Mohammed Saud S Algthlani | Noise Coming From Other Room

Families with children should, whenever possible, be assigned to designated family-friendly areas or grouped on specific floors to limit disturbance to other guests. Additionally, guests seeking a quieter stay (e.g., solo travelers, business guests) should be pre-assigned rooms away from high-traffic or family-occupied zones.

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained that his brand  new Porsche Cayenne was scratched upon check out after 24 hours in our car park

The hostess welcomed her promptly,  and the headwaiter quickly took the initial drink order.

A few minutes later,  the guest requested afternoon tea as well as dessert. The headwaiter informed her that we would be pleased to serve one afternoon tea,  along with a selection of desserts available from our offerings (including the Pause Gourmande and à la carte options),  instead of 4 afternoon tea.

Case closed. Extra care until departure.

-On Saturday 18 April,  Dr Alsugair had an appointment for treatments costing €550.
- We called reception to request authorisation to charge this amount to his room. 
-Reception informed us that the guest had to pay for his spa treatments at the spa. 
-When we asked the guest to pay the €550,  he was surprised and stated that nobody  had  informed him that his expenses could no longer be charged to his room. The guest was not happy. 
-We suggested to Dr Alsugair that we ask reception to go to the spa so that he could add money to his account. He refused and went back to his room to fetch his credit card so that he could pay directly at the spa.

awaiting a solution

rows.Incident Description: concierge waiting time & arrival experiences
rows.Subject: 132 | Mr. Max Carlo Klinke | Overall Incident
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:

A follow-up email was then sent to Guest Relations by the travel agent.

Investigation:
The guest was dissatisfied with the response time from Concierge. The team had been making efforts to secure a dinner reservation as requested; however,  L’OB was fully booked. They then attempted to arrange an aperitif reservation instead. Due to the high volume of requests and the ongoing efforts to secure options,  the response was not as prompt as expected.

During check-in,  the receptionist had introduced the hotel’s facilities and benefits. However,  the guest declined further information regarding restaurant options at that time.

Follow up:
GR reassured the guest via message and invited him to enjoy a tour of the hotel at his convenience. The guest subsequently received confirmation for an aperitif table at L’OB,  along with the possibility of dining should a table become available after the first seating. The guest appreciated the follow-up and expressed satisfaction with our professionalism.

A romantic turndown has been arranged during their outing this evening (guests' 3 months' anniversary),  and a departure gift is being prepared.

The guest will be met upon departure.

GR also responded to the travel agent by email to reassure them that the situation had improved. The agent was pleased and expressed appreciation for our partnership.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Always reconfirm with guests wether he requires further assistance/information when finishing the escort to room

rows.Incident Description: miscommunication
rows.Subject: 132 | Mr. Max Carlo Klinke | Treatment Quality
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The guest contacted Guest Relations to inform that his girlfriend was at the Spa and might require assistance due to a language barrier with the hairdresser. GR immediately went to the Spa with the Spa receptionist to assess the situation.

Investigation:
Mr. had originally booked appointments for both himself and his partner for a blow-dry. His partner begins the session first. During the service,  Mrs. requested a hair color; however,  the hairdresser understood this as a gloss treatment in connection with the blow-dry. This misunderstanding was due to the language barrier(guest prefers to communicate in English). In fact,  Mrs. wished to have a color and a blow-dry. 
Mr. also later changed his service to a haircut and blow-dry. Therefore,  the services were modified during the appointment compared to the initial booking.

Our hairdresser kindly extended her time in order to accommodate the guests’ updated requests. It is noted that both Mr. and Mrs. changed their appointments,  and the hairdresser remained to ensure their satisfaction.

Guests were left happily.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1:
Where possible
-it is best to speak directly to the person requesting an appointment to ensure they are choosing the right treatment.
-Also, if there is a language barrier, do not hesitate to ask colleagues who speak multiple languages for help.
-If no one is available who speaks the client’s language, do not hesitate to use a tablet to translate, to ensure that you fully understand the client’s requests.

rows.Incident Description:
Madam came at the lobby for a 8 people dinner organized by the lobby and sales team. 

Madam was disappointed about the delay of service and confusion in the menu that has been served.
 
The guest is in a "calm" behaviour.
rows.Subject: Le Lobby Restaurant | Ms. Aizhan Danyshpanova | Food / Beverage Service Delay
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The reservation was initially made for eight guests. The party arrived at the lobby at approximately 8:15 PM,  and the dinner was ultimately held for seven guests,  with the main guest arriving around 8:00 PM. Upon arrival,  she was promptly welcomed with champagne and water as a gesture of goodwill by the sales team. 

Service was delayed due to the late arrival of the seventh guest,  which postponed the start of the dinner. During this time,  the main guest expressed impatience regarding the timing of the starters,  stating: “they are the same starters for everyone anyway, ” which created some confusion among the team. She was informed that the starters were about to be served,  and in order to provide comfort during the wait,  four Bellota ham slates were offered to the table.

The starters,  including the asparagus,  were then served and the service proceeded smoothly at that stage.

At the main course stage,  when the poultry dish was served,  the guest raised a concern,  stating that two different pre-ordered menus had been requested. It was clarified that while two menu options had initially been requested,  her earlier confirmation that the starters were identical for all guests led the team to understand that a single menu had been selected for the entire table.

Dessert service followed,  including a birthday celebration with a candle presentation. A complimentary chocolate fondant and macarons were offered for the occasion.

The guest consumed Ruinart champagne throughout the dinner.

-The WhatsApp  is forwarded to the spa Director

-Explain the cancellation policy to the guest verbally
-Send a written confirmation to the guest’s room setting out the cancellation policy and also record it in Daylight
rows.Feedback Remarks 2: Ensure that the cancellation policy is always clearly stated and included in the confirmation letter.

rows.Incident Description: Guest complained to Front Desk Agent about her experience in an F&B outlet
rows.Subject: Others | Ms. Meng Meng Wang | Food / Beverage Service Delay
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Guest came to the front desk early in the evening to complain about her experience when she went to have a drink at an F&B outlet. 

She stated:
- That she had to wait a very long time to order a second drink
- That she had to ask to pay her bill several times,  so she went up to the counter herself to pay. 

(There is some uncertainty regarding the specific outlet due to the language barrier,  as after describing the guests at the Bar and the Lobby,  none of the staff members recalled seeing them. Since the guest paid directly on site,  it is difficult to identify the outlet)
Extra care until guest check-out. Guest are leaving at 12h01 on 26.04

Follow-up
The guest was met by GR at check-out and reported dissatisfaction with her experience at the Terrace of Bar Kléber,  citing long waiting times for both ordering and payment,  as well as discomfort caused by a guest smoking a cigar nearby,  which led them to leave quickly.

She also mentioned a less comfortable arrival experience,  noting the lack of assistance with luggage and no door service,  resulting in a feeling of not being taken care of.

GR extended sincere apologies and confirmed that the feedback would be shared with the relevant departments and management.

As recovery,  GR escorted the guest to L’Oiseau Blanc for lunch and briefed the team. The guest was very satisfied with the experience and appreciated the gesture of a hot drink and chocolate pageboy. 

The guest went to the spa following lunch. The spa team was informed of the situation and ensured the guest received attentive care throughout the treatment.

Guests received beauty products and an excused card  from GR when leaving the hotel.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1:
Set clear service-time standards for drink orders and bill settlement, and ensure staff proactively check on guests to avoid repeated requests. Reinforce accountability through regular floor supervision and quick-response protocols during peak hours.
To prevent similar situations, it is recommended to reinforce the presence and attentiveness of the Concierge/Bell team at the entrance, particularly during peak arrival times. Team members should proactively greet guests, assist with luggage, and ensure a smooth handover to the Front Desk.

rows.Incident Description: The guest had a reservation at 9:30pm but arrived at 10:30pm, by which time the kitchen was already closed.
rows.Subject: Le Lobby Restaurant | Amina  Messadoui | No Show Booking
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The guest made a reservation for 9:30 PM via an external concierge service. As no personal email address or phone number was provided,  we were unable to contact the guest in advance.

The guest arrived at 10:30 PM,  at which time the kitchen was already closed. The guest stated that,  according to our website,  the kitchen was scheduled to close at 11:00 PM. The Assistant Manager clarified the situation and presented the correct information on the lobby website to confirm that the kitchen had indeed closed.

As an alternative,  the Assistant Manager offered availability at Restaurant Lili or the room service menu at Bar Kléber. Both options were declined by the guest. The Assistant Manager also proposed to reschedule the reservation to another day; however,  this option was refused by the guests

The guests left unhappy.

Internal investigation revealed that reservation was made by a new external concierge service and entered into SevenRooms by the GCC. Unfortunately,  GCC staff failed to create a new profile for the concierge service,  preventing the F&B teams to contact the guests about their reservation status. SevenRooms profile has now been created and updated accordingly by GCC.
rows.Feedback Remarks 1:
Contact information to always be provided on SevenRooms when making a F&B booking.
In case of a reservation made by an external concierge service, their contact should be provided in spite of the guests'.

Guests came to the concierge desk this afternoon to complain about their breakfast experience at the Bar Kleber:

Reinforce coordination between outlets and attentive follow-up to address dissatisfaction in real time rather than post-experience.

The guest reported that an individual near the Lobby elevator entered the lift with her after she went out to smoke but exited before the doors closed to take the other elevator. 

She raised the concern as she was unsure whether the person was a hotel guest. 

Following a security check,  it was confirmed that the individual was waiting for Mr Shiff staying in room 405 and had briefly entered the wrong elevator by mistake.

GCC left a message for the guest to reassure her
To be met by a manager at checkout 

Guest was met by AFDM upon C/O 
She was thankful for the follow up 
Closed

rows.Incident Description: Room not ready upon arrival
rows.Subject: 430 | Dr. Xiaofei Li | Room Not Ready
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Informative

Guests arrived at the hotel at 6.25pm. ETA noted in the reservation was 7pm. The room was getting controlled at the time. 

Chinese speaker FD agent apologised for the delay and offered drinks at the bar while the final touched were done in the room. Timing given to the guest 6.45pm. 

The room was ready at 6.45pm but guests were enjoying their time at the Bar and they were in no rush to go up to the room. 

CLOSED

rows.Incident Description: A discrepancy occurred between the agency’s expectations and the final setup, as the delivered décor—particularly the florals and table presentation was more minimal than anticipated and did not fully reflect the shared visual references within the agreed scope.
rows.Subject: General misunderstanding between the agency’s request and the proposed offer.
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
A gap was observed between the expectations expressed by the agency and the final delivery. A detailed brief,  visual references,  and several validation points were shared in advance. The setup delivered (including florals and table presentation) was perceived as more minimal than expected.

The visual references were used as inspiration and were not fully reflected within the validated scope of delivery.
The selected package,  including the floral add-on,  did not include all elements shown in the shared references as it was understood that a rose petal arrangement would be sufficient.

This resulted in a difference between the expected setup and the delivered setup on the day of the event
Despite the explanations provided,  the client remains very dissatisfied.
Valentin is awaiting her next response.

Closed but Internal investigation to be done
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: Following an internal review, managers must verify the communications between their hostesses and end clients to ensure the promised delivery is accurate and that all emails are properly reviewed before being sent.

Unfortunately,  nothing has been found since all linen were already taken by the outside company. Follow up to be done by HSK Manager in the morning. Guest is checking out at 9:45am and to be met by AFDM/HSK Manager to inform about the outcome of our investigations.

rows.Incident Description: Complained that the room hadn't been cleaned even though they had requested it on the WhatsApp group
rows.Subject: 440 | Ms. Fenzhen Du | Miscommunication
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Mr. Xu called from room #439 to ask why rooms #439 and #440 were not yet cleaned (as he had requested them to be cleaned for 10.30 am). 

GCC apologized and asked if he wanted their rooms to be cleaned right away.

 He accepted and wanted to be sure that his comment was well noted for next time.

FYI : There is a WhatsApp group for this guets where they are very active; unfortunately,  the information was not seen when it was shared. 
Also housekeeping was not on this group 

Update recovery : Apology note in chinese will be placed in the room with hermes toiletries on 01.05 & departure transfer for 02.05 for his son will be offered as gesture.
Apology note was not placed as per HSK as the room was on DND 
Guests met at departure and they seem to be happy with their stay. 
Closed
rows.Feedback Remarks 1: ensure efficient follow up of the guest's requests via different platforms

rows.Incident Description: Guest was not pleased with the gluten free birthday cake made for his girl friend birthday
rows.Subject: 418 | Mr. Gustavo Gutierrez CONFIDENTIAL | Miscommunication
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
On Monday 27th April Guest asked the Concierge team to organize a vanilla gluten-free cake with a bit of raspberry for his girlfriend ‘s birthday on Wednesday 29th April -guest sent pictures of expected cake
The cake was arranged from an outside bakery who can provide the gluten free product.
The cake was made on time and delivered to the suite on April 29th.
On the departure date guest complained to the Head Concierge that the cake was not what he was asking and there was too many raspberries and not enough vanilla. He wanted to have a vanilla flavour and hardly a bit of raspberry.
Apologies extended by the Head Concierge,  taxi and the cake fare have been refunded from his final bill.

rows.Incident Description: One of the event’s guests expressed disappointment with the quality of the pastries (externally sourced) provided for the “Lemon Lane” service.
rows.Subject: 634 | Ms. Laura Charlotte Redman | Food / Beverage Quality
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
A meeting was held today in a guest room and managed by the banquet team. For this occasion,  pastries were sourced externally rather than prepared within the establishment. After tasting them,  one of the clients expressed disappointment with their quality and went out to purchase his own pastries outside the hotel.

The banquet team did attempt to offer homemade pastries,  but the client declined and stated that he was surprised to be offered pastries of such poor quality in a Parisian palace.

The rest of the event went as smoothly as possible,  and the clients and organizers left satisfied.

Closed but internal investigation to be done

rows.Incident Description: Guest disputed breakfast charges upon departure
rows.Subject: Reception Desk | Jaap Van Zweden | Breakfast Inclusion
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Guest met with DGR during check out and disputed the breakfast charges of 525€ upon departure.

Mrs told us everyday the Lobby team informed her that breakfast was included and a signature was just needed to check the delivery items.

She was surprised about those charges that appeared on the bill.

Apologies extended by DGR and 525€  were deducted exceptionally.

Guest left very happy with the gesture. 

Following our investigation,  no manager or hostess informed the guest that breakfast was included. It appears that a miscommunication may have occurred with a chef de rang when the bill was presented on the first day.

To prevent similar issues in the future,  an improved verification process regarding included or non-included breakfast will be implemented at the lobby desk.
Additionally,  the chef de rang will update and standardize their communication to ensure clarity when presenting the bill.
